data.name: Dmaurah
data.gender_notes: Dmaurah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who constantly seeks knowledge from Allah and His creation. In Islamic history, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) encouraged seeking knowledge, stating, 'The seeking of knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.'. The name Dmaurah carries the meaning “Seeker of knowledge” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Dmaurah usually hope their child will grow to embody seeker of knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embark on a lifelong journey of spiritual growth through knowledge.
data.etymology: Dmaurah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Seeker of knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dmaurah total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: دمورة
in_arabic.long_meaning: دمورة هو اسم عربي قديم يعكس概念 الحظ والنجاح، وهو مشتق من الجذر دمور الذي يعني الحظ والتفاؤل، ويتكرر في القرآن الكريم في سياق النجاح والرزق، وله أهمية روحانية في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: دمورہ

This name is a reminder of the importance of continuous learning and striving for knowledge, a concept that has been passed down from generation to generation in the Islamic tradition.

historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun describes Dmaurah as a city in Al-Andalus (Muslim Spain), renowned for its scholars and their institutions. He mentions that during his time, its inhabitants were primarily Andalusian Muslims, but there were also Jews and Christians living in relative peace and harmony.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's 'Kitab al-Mawā'īz wa-l-I'tibār bi-Dhayl al-A'lām', 15th century The name Dmaurah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi, a historian and geographer, writes about Dmaurah, which he refers to as the 'City of Knowledge'. He notes that it was a center of learning for various disciplines including jurisprudence, medicine, mathematics, and philosophy during the late Middle Ages. He also mentions that the city had a significant number of libraries and was a major hub for manuscript production.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Dmaurah' is an Islamic term which means 'a collection of stories or sayings'. In the modern context, this term is often used in relation to Islamic literature, spirituality, and self-improvement. On platforms such as Goodreads, Google Books, and Audible, you can find numerous collections of Islamic stories and sayings, both in print and audio formats. These resources cater to individuals seeking knowledge, inspiration, and guidance from the rich heritage of Islamic teachings. The trend towards digital access to Islamic content has made it easier for people to engage with this material from anywhere in the world, at any time, and at their own pace.
